subject: RFP — Dedicated inference capacity: GPU fitment, burst policy, and throughput assumptions

Subject: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity - questionnaire attached

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is CloudWave_RFP_V2.xlsx — our procurement team condensed our asks into the capacity worksheet we typically use. High level: we expect 150k peak tokens/minute for text-generation features (chat + assistant), 40k embedding requests/day (batch), and 95th p90 latency targets of <120ms for conversational requests.

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood provide recommended GPU mix for a dedicated pool that meets the above?
- How do you size reservation vs. burst capacity (we expect spikes up to 3x baseline during launches)?
- Any known kernel/compatibility constraints for our model stack (custom LLM forks + quantized variants)?

We hope to collect responses by EOD 18 Jun to feed the procurement review. Please attach any profiling or math you used.

Attachment: CloudWave_RFP_V2.xlsx (xlsx)

Regards,

Hi Rajesh — thanks for the worksheet. We're happy to respond; attaching our RFI template (rfi_capacity_template.xlsx) to capture a couple of workload details that weren't in your sheet (typical sequence length distribution, request concurrency during business hours, and cold-start patterns). A couple of quick clarifying asks before we run full sizing:

1) When you say "150k peak tokens/minute" — is that sustained peak over 5 minutes or a 1-minute instantaneous spike?
2) Are conversational requests single-turn (system+user) or do they include long history (10+ turns) for KV cache sizing?
3) For embeddings: do those arrive as continuous streams (steady background batch) or short bursts tied to indexing jobs?

I'll do an initial pass with conservative assumptions (5-minute sustained peak, average seq length 256 tokens, 1.8x packing for multi-request packing) and loop Marcus and Karthik for GPU fitment.

Subject: RE: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity - questionnaire attached

Olga / team — did a sizing sketch based on the conservative assumptions Olga listed (5-min sustained peak, avg seq 256, 1.8x packing). Key recommendations and rationale below. I also attached profiler output we ran against CloudWave's model family (profiler_output_20260609.json).

Summary recommendation (baseline reservation + burst):
- Baseline reserved pool: 20 x A100-80GB (mixed-precision fp16) serving as primary low-latency pool. Expected sustained throughput: ~125k tokens/min (with request-level batching/packing).
- Burst buffer: 12 x H100-80GB (on-demand burst nodes) to handle up to 2.5-3x spikes; used primarily for long-history chat requests where KV cache footprint grows.
- Cost-optimized archival ops and large-batch embedding jobs: L40S instances for batch embedding workers (4 x L40S recommended for the 40k/day workload if embeddings are batched overnight).

Sizing math (high level):
- Single A100-80GB perf: ~6,200 tokens/sec for 256-token sequences (fp16, Redwood runtime continuous-batching). That maps to ~372k tokens/min per A100. Accounting for realistic packing inefficiencies, tail latency SLOs, and multi-tenant safety factor, use 18% effective utilization -> ~67k tokens/min per A100 baseline.
- To hit 150k tokens/min sustained, 3 baseline A100s would be required by raw math, but for redundancy, headroom, and maintenance windows we recommend 20 reserved A100s (this supports the customer's concurrency SLO and gives us capacity to shift lower-priority jobs).
- Burst policy: keep H100s as a warm pool that can be autoscaled into within 60s for heavy spikes; because H100s have better per-GPU throughput for int8/4 quantized paths, the burst pool lets you keep lower reservation footprint.

Deployment notes / tradeoffs:
- Kernel compatibility: most common LLama-derived forks and quantized checkpoints are supported; the runtime will select int8/4 kernels when available. However, custom fused ops or altered attention variants may need a short onboarding pass (we estimate 2-3 days engineering support).
- KV cache memory: long-history conversations (10+ turns) increase per-request KV cache by ~1.4–2.2x; plan reserve slots to avoid eviction-induced tail latencies.
- Packing: we assume a production packing ratio of 1.8x; if your traffic is highly bursty per user, packing falls and you need more reserve.

Attachments referenced: profiler_output_20260609.json (JSON), rough-sim spreadsheet (I will include in final response).

Bottom line proposal for procurement doc: reserve 20 A100s + 4 L40S for batch + contract option to burst up to 12 H100s for product launches. We can provide a tiered pricing worksheet that shows committed monthly and burst hour prices.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity - questionnaire attached

Quick compliance thread — copying here so procurement sees the notes in Olga's consolidated reply.

- Data residency: confirm whether CloudWave requires customer data to remain in a specific region; dedicated deployments support VPC/private options and regional pinning but we need to know region to guarantee KMS/HSM key locality.
- Audit logs: Redwood Private can push audit logs to your SIEM or to a customer-owned S3. We retain inference-level logs for 30 days by default but can extend to 1 year under SOC2+ contracts.
- FIPS / Gov-style requirements: If CloudWave needs FIPS 140-2 validated crypto or FIPS-approved kernels, we need to flag that immediately — some cloud regions' GPU drivers and kernel builds differ and can add 2–4 weeks to compliance validation.
- Multi-tenant isolation: for an enterprise reserved pool we recommend single-tenant node allocation for sensitive workloads; that affects packing ratios and increases reserved count by ~10–15%.

If you want I can draft a compliance addendum we can attach to the RFP response.

—Neha
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

Subject: Consolidated RFP response: reservation tiers, GPU fitment & next steps

Rajesh — please find our consolidated responses below and attached files (redwood_capacity_response_20260618.xlsx, kernel_compatibility_notes.pdf). We tried to keep the procurement worksheet numbers conservative and transparent.

What we've attached:
- redwood_capacity_response_20260618.xlsx: line-item reservation recommendation (20 x A100-80GB baseline; 4 x L40S for batch embedding; optional 12 x H100 burst buffer) and tiered pricing (committed vs. burst hourly).
- kernel_compatibility_notes.pdf: short technical note about model families we profiled and known edge cases for custom fused ops.

Short answers to your Qs:
- Baseline vs burst: we propose a committed baseline sized for typical day-to-day traffic and a warm burst pool for product launches. Baseline is sized for 5-minute sustained peaks; burst covers up to 3x instantaneous spikes with ~60s ramp.
- Model/kernel compatibility: majority supported; custom ops may require engineering onboarding (2–3 days). We included the profiler output we used.
- Embeddings: if you can batch embedding jobs to off-peak windows, L40S nodes reduce cost materially.

Next steps:
1) If the sizing worksheet looks good, we'd like to run a 90-minute sizing workshop with your infra and models on Mon 22 Jun or Tue 23 Jun to validate sequence distributions and run a small canary.
2) Procurement / legal: we'll attach a compliance addendum per Neha's note if you need extended audit retention or FIPS validation.

Doc links: https://hubspot.redwood/records/CW-8742 (for procurement team)

Attachments: redwood_capacity_response_20260618.xlsx (xlsx), kernel_compatibility_notes.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop,
